headline: High-risk workspace overlap: Cline can write and execute in the workspace while LlamaFactory is non-interactive, making prompt injection and data leakage plausible but not default-critical.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Cline can read/write workspace files, use MCP, and run browsers; if LlamaFactory consumes shared workspace artifacts or generated outputs, injected instructions could cross the boundary. LlamaFactory itself has no I/O surfaces, so the pathway is one-way and not proven by docs, but the shared-filesystem model makes it plausible.
conditions: IF LlamaFactory is configured to ingest workspace files produced by Cline
IF Cline writes attacker-controlled content into files that LlamaFactory later parses as instructions
mitigations: Separate workspaces for the two agents
Disable file-based handoff between agents
Require human review of any Cline-generated prompt or config before reuse
Use allowlisted file types only
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging on shared artifacts

B_data_leakage.rationale: Cline touches source code and browser screenshots and shares state via filesystem; if LlamaFactory is pointed at the same workspace, sensitive code or screenshots can be exposed through file handoff. LlamaFactory has no network egress or file access by default, so leakage is not automatic, but the shared workspace makes it plausible in default coding setups.
conditions: IF both agents are run in the same VS Code workspace
IF Cline writes browser screenshots or source code into files that LlamaFactory reads
mitigations: Use separate OS users or workspaces
Keep screenshots and secrets out of shared folders
Turn off automatic file ingestion for LlamaFactory
Review workspace permissions before launch
requires-engineering: add per-agent access controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Cline has broad write and git capabilities, while LlamaFactory has no write, shell, or network capabilities. That makes direct capability conflict minimal; the only overlap is read-only absence on B, so there is no meaningful concurrent write contention.
conditions: IF LlamaFactory is granted new write or git permissions outside the profile
mitigations: Keep LlamaFactory read-only
Avoid running both agents against the same git branch
Use separate working copies
requires-engineering: add workspace locking if B gains writes

D_cascading_error.rationale: Cline can generate code, browser-derived content, and file outputs that LlamaFactory could treat as input if wired together. Because LlamaFactory has no documented verification or action-taking surface, the cascade is plausible but not proven; uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF LlamaFactory consumes Cline-produced files without an explicit verification step
IF Cline's browser-derived outputs are used as authoritative facts downstream
mitigations: Insert a human verification step between agents
Pass only structured, schema-validated outputs
Reject free-form text as machine input
Log source provenance for each handoff
requires-engineering: add automated consistency checks

E_compliance.rationale: Cline handles model-provider API keys and browser screenshots, while LlamaFactory is documented as touching no data classes and has no network or file surfaces. No specific residency or certification mismatch is evidenced, so compliance risk is limited to local handling gaps rather than a documented breach pathway.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into Cline's workspace or browser screenshots
IF LlamaFactory is later configured to store or transmit that regulated data
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the shared workspace
Redact screenshots before saving
Use separate retention policies per agent
Document data-handling boundaries
requires-engineering: map residency and retention controls
